title: Waveform-sequencing for scanning tunneling microscopy based pump-probe spectroscopy and pulsed-ESR
author: Natterer

steps.title: Install transfer relay in bias line
steps.instruction: Insert a PCB‑mount relay (Tianbo) into the bias‑voltage path of the STM control electronics, solder BNC connectors to the relay contacts, and power the relay with a 5 V USB supply; the relay will act as a mechanical transfer switch between the DC bias and the AWG pulse output.

steps.title: Connect AWG and optional RF generator
steps.instruction: Wire the arbitrary waveform generator (AWG) to the STM control electronics as shown in Fig. 1 (red lines) and, if desired, add the RF generator (Keysight N5183B) via the dashed yellow connections; the AWG output and the RF generator share the same cabling to the STM box, while the relay selects either the DC bias or the AWG pulses for the STM bias line.

steps.title: Create pump and probe waveforms (arbs)
steps.instruction: Using MATLAB, generate three arbitrary waveforms (arbs): pump arb P (arbP) and two probe arbs A and B (arbA, arbB). Each arb must have equal sample length l = t_arb × SR, where SR is the AWG sample‑rate. Design the total arb duration t_arbA to be several times the expected relaxation time of the system. Set arbA to a 10 ns, 50 mV pulse, arbB = ‑arbA, and arbP to a 5 ns, 150 mV pulse. All three arbs have a total duration of 50 ns.

steps.title: Configure waveform sequencing and sync signal
steps.instruction: Program the AWG to play the probe arbs cyclically on Channel 1 at approximately f_cycle = 887 Hz for lock‑in detection. Build a playlist consisting of N segments of arbA (cycle A) followed by N segments of arbB (cycle B), where N = 1 / (2 f_cycle t_arbA). Set the AWG sync output high during cycle A and low during cycle B. Note that the effective f_cycle may be reduced by rounding down N.

steps.title: Play pump arb continuously on Channel 2
steps.instruction: Configure Channel 2 of the AWG to output arbP perpetually; the AWG internally adds Channel 1 and Channel 2 and delivers the combined signal on output 1 to the STM bias line.

steps.title: Set phase modulation for time‑delay control
steps.instruction: Connect the Mod‑In input of the AWG to an external DC control voltage (V_ctr) from the STM control electronics (or a DAQ card). Vary V_ctr between ‑5 V and +5 V to shift the phase of arbP by ‑180° to +180°, which circularly moves the 5 ns pump pulse within its 50 ns arb and thus scans the pump‑probe delay Δt over the full t_arbA range. Phase can also be set via computer control of the AWG.

steps.title: Set amplitude modulation for pump amplitude
steps.instruction: Use the amplitude‑modulation (AM) input of the AWG, driven by the same V_ctr, to adjust the pump‑pulse amplitude: V_ctr = +5 V yields the maximal positive amplitude, V_ctr = ‑5 V yields the maximal negative amplitude. This mode is useful for locating threshold voltages of dynamical processes.

steps.title: Validate timing with Schottky diode junction
steps.instruction: Replace the STM tip with a Schottky diode (Pasternack PE8014) to act as a nonlinear tunneling junction. Overlap pump and probe pulses; the diode’s nonlinearity produces an extra current when the pulses coincide, allowing assessment of the system’s time resolution and detection of impedance mismatches.

steps.title: Perform DC pump–probe correlation measurements
steps.instruction: With both pump and probe pulses generated as DC pulses, keep the probe width fixed at 10 ns and vary the pump‑pulse width t_pump from 5 ns to 15 ns. Record the diode current versus relative delay to obtain the cross‑correlation trace.

steps.title: Configure RF pump with DC probe pulses
steps.instruction: Route Channel 2 directly to the pulse‑trigger input of the RF generator (Keysight N5183B). Keep Channel 1 playing only the probe‑pulse sequence (arbA/arbB). The RF generator should be set to 20 GHz frequency and –5 dBm output power. The RF pulses travel through a resistive bias‑tee (Tektronix PSPL5370) to the junction and overlap with the DC probe pulses (still 10 ns). Vary the RF‑pulse width t_pump from 5 ns to 25 ns while recording the diode correlation signal.

steps.title: Analyze correlation curves for edge times and ringing
steps.instruction: Examine the shape of the correlation traces: edge times of ~3 ns indicate the AWG speed limit; any dip at negative delays (as seen in the RF case) signals ringing caused by impedance mismatches such as the bias‑tee’s 450 Ω pick‑off impedance.

steps.title: Measure cable‑length‑dependent delay and propagation
steps.instruction: Insert cable segments of known lengths into the Channel 2 pulse path and measure the shift of the correlation‑maximum with a precision of 30 ps. From the linear dependence obtain a propagation time of (4.98 ± 0.06) ns m⁻¹, a velocity factor of (0.671 ± 0.008), and a sensitivity to length changes of about 6 mm.
